newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate eases, baht up late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate eases, baht up late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate eased further late on Monday while baht firmed against a weaker dollar, dealers said.

Dealers said ample liquidity, boosted by a return of funds withdrawn for the holiday season and cash fleeing a battered stock market, pushed the overnight rate down to 10.25-10.50 percent from 11.00-11.50 in the morning.

"The rate could drop further on Tuesday. Most banks have already met reserve requirements, so they will likely offer aggressively tomorrow...anyway, it depends on the dollar tone too," said a dealer at a major Thai bank.
The baht rallied sharply to 25.623/25.633 to the dollar from 25.655/25.660 in the morning after comments by a senior Japanese finance ministry official triggered heavy dollar selling.
"The baht took a cue from lower dollar/yen which dropped after comments by Ogawa," a dealer said, referring to Japan Vice Minister Tadashi Ogawa.
The bid/offer range of one-month dollar/baht swap premium fell to 8.50/9.50 satangs per dollar from 9.50/10.50 in the morning in line with lower Thai interbank rates, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed dollar/baht midrate at 25.65 against 25.60 on Friday. -- Anchalee Koetsawang (662) 652-0642
